literal: Affection, knowledge, clarity, desire-absence, these four-all, well he-who-possesses with-indeed trust.
translation: Trust should be placed only in someone who fully possesses all these four qualities: loyalty, knowledge, clear judgment, and freedom from greed.
modern: அன்பு, அறிவு, தெளிந்த சிந்தனை, பேராசை இல்லாமை ஆகிய இந்த நான்கு பண்புகளையும் தன்னிடம் முழுமையாகக் கொண்டிருப்பவரிடமே ஒரு செயலை ஒப்படைக்கும் நம்பிக்கையை வைக்க வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet lists the four essential qualities a leader must look for before trusting someone with a responsibility. The person must have 'அன்பு' (loyalty or affection) towards the leader or the cause, and 'அறிவு' (knowledge) to understand and execute the tasks. They must also possess 'தேற்றம்' (clarity of mind or clear judgment) and 'அவாவின்மை' (the absence of greed), ensuring they will not be confused or corrupted. The word 'தெளிவு' signifies the clear decision to trust and delegate, which should rest solely ('கட்டே') with one who has all four traits fully ('நன்கு').
